ideas.title: The bent wire that spins by itself
ideas.nearest: A copper wire keeps its bends
ideas.critique: The first electromagnetism on the island, and the payoff (your own bend spins, wobbles off or won't start) is new and could be clipped. It builds on the wire bench without repeating it. The danger is a motor that spins at a fitted speed whatever shape you bend: the three bends in the film have to differ because of their geometry and friction, not because the script says so.

ideas.title: Skip a stone you chipped
ideas.nearest: Skipping stones, a take that misses
same_form: A snowball that grows as it rolls, a take that misses
ideas.critique: It is a retake of a failed post, this time with a real mechanism: planing impacts from the stone's own chipped underside are a real step past rings appearing on the sea. The film is still one thrown object with rings on water, which the island has shown, and an unseen stone will repeat the old miss.

ideas.title: A log that rocks when a friend climbs in
ideas.critique: The next step of the log-boat project, and the hull answering moving weight is a real addition to static floating. The payoff is still a log settling at a slant in the sea, one post after the last log film. Friends as point masses sliding on a deck will read as toys pushed around unless their bodies climb and shift.

ideas.title: Pull a stone up with two pulleys
ideas.nearest: A copper wire keeps its bends
ideas.critique: Rope over wheels is new to the island, but mechanical advantage is a textbook demo whose ending everyone already knows, and 'Lumi's pull limited to its strength' risks being a single number that decides the scene. It has little to do with making things that keep their marks.

ideas.title: A reed whistle you carve
ideas.nearest: Chipping a stone to change its note
same_form: Chipping a stone to change its note
ideas.critique: A note solved from a thing's shape is the island's third sound post in ten. A bore with holes is a different acoustic system from knocked modes, and a playable instrument is a real goal. 'Friends dance to it' is where it slides into a scripted scene, and a synthesized tone with a pitch table attached is the plain version people will hear.

ideas.title: Paint that drips and stays
ideas.critique: Paint that stays permanently, with thin-film drips, is strong to play and something the engine has never had. But it carries out the human's own named example (the spray can), so it cannot surprise anyone who has read the goals. Persistence across the whole island is the hard part, and also the part that matters.

ideas.title: Lumi falls for real
ideas.critique: An active ragdoll for the hero would change how every film feels and serves the animation goal. But there is nothing for a player to do with it except watch, and balance controllers usually come out as flailing or stiff toppling. Making it fail well is the whole job.

ideas.title: A coil that grabs nails
ideas.nearest: A copper wire keeps its bends
ideas.critique: Biot-Savart from the real winding path is genuine physics, but an electromagnet picking up nails is the most predictable demo of it, and it pitches itself as second to the motor. Switching it on and off is fun once, and the pieces will jump unless the force from the field gradient is handled carefully.

ideas.title: Fold a paper boat and race the stream
ideas.critique: Folding plus paper slowly soaking and slumping is a fresh material behaviour and lands close to the big goal's paper. But floating by hull.jl is the payoff the last post already showed, and 'crease angles' is vague enough that the plain version is a few preset boat shapes.

ideas.title: Pound clay into a brick and build a wall
ideas.critique: Stiffness that depends on water content and a stagger that holds are real ideas. But a rigid-body brick wall falling over is the most familiar physics demo there is, and laying bricks one by one gets tedious fast. Brick creep is the only thing here nobody has seen, and it is the part most likely to be faked.
